1: Inspect first: record staged/untracked paths and current branch; save a reviewed checkpoint plan without adding source or secrets. Record the evidence file as a documentation-only commit.
Existing source paths remain staged/untracked exactly as before; checkpoint plan names the work to preserve.
Record available disk and the agreed cleanup owner. Do not delete files automatically. Stop image pulls until at least 30 GiB is free.
Available column proves at least 30 GiB, or the gate records BLOCKED and no image is pulled.
Inspect installed JDKs with /usr/libexec/java_home -V; select an installed Java 21 in this shell/IDE or record the installation blocker. Do not change the project Java target to 17.
Version line contains major 21; a different major leaves this prerequisite blocked.
After the disk gate, start the installed Docker Desktop normally; record daemon version and memory allocation. Do not start PostgreSQL/Kafka yet.
Server section responds without a daemon-socket error; no business/database port is published.

Inspect pom.xml and all seven service poms plus shared libraries. Time-box resolution/compile of current reactor under Java 21; record Boot/Cloud/Avro versions, compatibility evidence and one smallest correction to make next. Output is a finding, not seven unreviewed pom edits.
Reactor lists ten projects and BUILD SUCCESS for validation; compilation is separately recorded and never inferred from validate.

Inspect first: use the spike findings to align this one service to the reviewed root baseline; replace JPA with JDBC and add the minimum test dependencies. Create the proposed context test using the actual existing IdentityOrgApplication. Do not align six other poms in this step.
Context test executes with Failures: 0; dependency tree has JDBC and no accidental Hibernate runtime for this owner.

Inspect first: switch this scaffold from MVC to the compatible reactive gateway dependency established by the spike. Add one context test; deny business routes until later verified routing/auth. No repository/database dependency belongs in this service.
Gateway context test passes on the reactive stack; no business route is open anonymously.
Test one diagnostic migration in PostgreSQL

Inspect first: if a migration already exists, select the next unused version instead of V1. In a disposable real PostgreSQL container create a non-personal diagnostic row, query it through JdbcClient and assert duplicate constraint failure. Keep it out of public business endpoints.
Real PostgreSQL test passes clean migration, one stored diagnostic row and rejected duplicate; H2 is not used.
Write the first versioned OpenAPI slice

Inspect first: confirm no wire-authority file exists. Create the proposed sole spec for /api/v1/departments with the golden-slice request and 201/400/401/403/problem examples; mark it planned, not deployed. Record a pinned validator command from its official documentation and run it.
Exactly one OpenAPI source is listed; its validator succeeds and a deliberate invalid local copy fails.
Retain and build the Nuxt client

Inspect web/package.json, package-lock.json and current welcome source. Replace only the welcome view with a minimal contract-fixture panel, retaining Nuxt/Vue and the matching lockfile. Do not rewrite web to React.
Nuxt build completes without error and the panel identifies its data as a fixture.
Locate or create the Flutter shell

Inspect first: locate an existing Flutter project before choosing mobile. If absent create a Flutter shell at proposed mobile, record flutter --version and lockfile, and keep one widget test. No backend call yet. Run flutter test from the confirmed mobile root.
Confirmed Flutter version/root recorded; one shell widget test passes and the emulator shows the shell.
Drive the mock from the one contract

Inspect the actual mobile root and pinned mock/validator from W01-S09. Start its local mock from the sole OpenAPI file, then make the Flutter fixture test assert the documented department response. Do not create a second independent mock schema.
Only the contract fixture and client test change; mock returns documented 201 fields and the client assertion passes.
Show one contract failure in both clients

Repeat the golden slice with delta: invalid department fixture returns the documented problem code; both clients display safe detail and preserve input. Verify no technical stack or token is rendered.
Nuxt build and selected Flutter test pass; invalid fixture displays VALIDATION_FAILED with no stack trace.
Add the shared problem contract to identity

Inspect first: locate any error advice. If absent use these proposed paths. Write a failing validation/error assertion, then return the golden problem shape with a stable code/traceId and application/problem+json. Keep unknown exceptions sanitized.
Validation and unexpected-error tests assert content type and standard members, with no exception/stack in the response.
Match the reactive gateway error shape
Inspect the actual reactive error hooks selected by W01-S07; write the equivalent problem body for a denied/unroutable request. Reuse wire fixtures; do not copy MVC advice into WebFlux.
Reactive error test matches the same problem fields and never serializes a stack trace.

Add the exact tested validation and sanitized-500 examples to the sole contract. Run its pinned validator and compare client fixtures; record the command/output instead of claiming an unused schema is checked.
Examples include stable codes and no secrets; validator and fixture assertions pass.
Prove failures cannot create diagnostic data

Extend the existing disposable PostgreSQL test with invalid insert and rollback assertions. A failed transaction must leave its original row count unchanged. Run the assertion red before the minimum fix if a defect is found.
Rejected input/rolled-back insert changes zero committed rows; all identity tests pass.

Inspect first: no formatter is inferred. Pin a compatible Spotless plugin/version after a small local trial, configure the existing Java roots, run check, then format only the touched future implementation files. A reviews the root-pom change inside the review allowance.
Formatting check succeeds on formatted input and fails on an intentionally unformatted temporary copy.
Fail static analysis on one real defect

Pin compatible PMD plugin/rules in the existing Maven build. Trial one synthetic unused/unsafe code fixture outside production; record rule ID and nonzero exit, then remove the fixture. Do not suppress all warnings to get green.
PMD check fails on its recorded bad fixture and succeeds after removal; actual build rules remain enabled.

Pin compatible JaCoCo and record the actual auth/attendance/leave domain/application package selectors. Set 80 percent lines and 70 percent branches on nonempty implemented critical packages; missing future packages are explicitly not covered, not reported as 100 percent.
Existing tests produce a report; a deliberate uncovered implemented critical branch fails the configured check.

Review the container fixture from W01-S08: pin PostgreSQL 16 image, use mapped connection details, and remove any fallback to H2 or silent skip when Docker is absent. Prove an invalid DB constraint reaches PostgreSQL.
Container-backed test passes; stopping Docker produces an environment failure, never a skipped success.
Inspect the existing Avro and listener paths

Read the actual avsc under libs/hrflow-contracts/events, libs poms and Compose. Record host/container listener addresses and SQL bind-mount source; identify Registry bootstrap mismatch without changing volumes.
Compose syntax exits zero; findings separately name bad mount/listener values because syntax validation does not prove connectivity.

After disk/Docker gates, use a disposable isolated broker/Registry environment to trial the exact serializer/runtime versions from the spike. Record accepted compatible evolution and rejected incompatible schema. Output is a finding, not a production publisher.
Finding records resolved versions, actual round-trip result or exact blocker; an unavailable image/dependency is not a business pass.
Record the first event round-trip result

Use only synthetic tenant/employee data and the inspected event schema in the isolated spike. Record produce/consume and a duplicate replay observation with a bounded wait. Explain why this is not yet outbox/inbox exactly-once processing.
Actual producer/consumer evidence is recorded or the spike is blocked; no durable business delivery is claimed.

Inspect actual jar names from Maven outputs. Add the two proposed Dockerfiles with pinned reviewed Java 21 runtime image digests, non-root users and no secrets; build each with the matching existing service context. Record digests, total size and memory gate. This does not prove the full seven-service host fits.
Both local candidate images build from reviewed jars, run as non-root and have recorded digests; absent/pull-failed images block the CI image-scan gate.
Make CI execute the same checks

Inspect first: create the proposed workflow only if no equivalent exists. Use Java 21, pinned action revisions and existing Maven/Nuxt commands plus contract/docs checks. Push to the authorized implementation work branch only; no deployment credentials.
Workflow names actual commands; a deliberately failing test blocks CI. Local YAML existence alone is not a CI pass.

Pin Gitleaks in the existing workflow and verify it detects its documented synthetic test-secret fixture in a temporary test repository. Do not add a real secret, disable scanning or print credentials.
Every push has secret scanning; the safe synthetic fixture fails and the real docs/code scan has recorded results.
Scan dependencies and the built image

Pin Trivy filesystem/dependency and image scans. Add the reviewed build step for the first identity image if its Dockerfile is already created; otherwise record the missing-image blocker and do not mark Q12 complete. Pin base image version/digest from registry evidence.
Workflow cannot report an absent image or failed scan database download as success; unresolved findings are explicit release blockers.

Inspect actual package/module dependencies. Time-box an ArchUnit proof against the nonempty identity test classes; a synthetic infrastructure import from domain must fail. Record proposed rules and exact test command for Week 3, not an empty-package green test.
Finding shows a forbidden edge fails and the clean equivalent passes, or records the exact spike blocker.
Use Thursday only to repair one blocker

Choose the earliest failed prerequisite, reproduce it with its original exact command and record one next action. No new feature, tool or concept today. If repair exceeds the slot, carry it forward and keep the gate failed.
Named earlier failure has a reproduction/result and owner; no missing quality check is silently deleted.
Re-run existing invalid/timeout fixture from the confirmed mobile root; assert retry preserves entered data and never loops. Record observed UI state with synthetic data. No new screen.
Existing client build and selected Flutter negative fixture pass; retry is bounded and safe.

Run the 10-minute shared checklist. Record every current image/config/migration/test ID and blocker. Stage explicit reviewed implementation paths only; never git add dot in a dirty workspace. Do not tag red work.
No whitespace errors; review and test reports identify a reproducible candidate or a failed gate.
Redeploy locally and record the gate

Redeploy only the reviewed private skeleton on the same confirmed local target; verify readiness/denied business routes and scratch dump restore of the disposable diagnostic DB. If scripts/images/host are not ready record the blocker instead. Decide gate, next exact action and stop for two rest days.
Private readiness, denied unauthenticated business access and scratch restore have actual evidence, or gate remains FAIL; no production-readiness claim.
2: Inspect identity and security before coding
Inspect existing Security configuration, user/refresh migrations, gateway filters and tests; record actual names or the proposed targets for this week. No endpoint/table is presumed present.
Inventory distinguishes existing scaffold from new auth targets and names the next failing test.

Inspect first: create proposed LoginTest if absent. Add a fixed synthetic active user fixture and assert valid login returns access-token response contract; do not implement login yet. Failed compilation is not a valid red result.
The login behavior assertion fails for missing response; red commit is not green-tagged or deployed.
Hash passwords behind one tested function
Use the existing Spring Security password encoder after inspecting its version; test matches/wrong password and unique salt. Never log/store plaintext or compare hashes as raw string equality.
Password tests pass, stored value differs from plaintext, wrong password fails; outstanding login red stays on work branch.
Add the minimal credential lookup and login

Inspect migrations first: choose next unused version if V2 is taken. Add tenant-scoped normalized credential lookup and use the password function. Token creation is an injected port filled next; do not return fake production tokens or an entity. Pre-auth lookup is a narrow audited exception, not arbitrary tenant business access.
Credential path works in the test fixture; absent token port leaves full login acceptance red until W02-S05.
Sign and validate the access-token claims

Load signing private key from environment/secret mount; sign short-lived asymmetric JWT, validate issuer/audience/signature/expiry in tests with test keys. Never put a production key in YAML. Wire the login port and run its original red assertion green.
Valid login returns a verified short-lived access token; expired/wrong-audience/wrong-key tests fail safely.
Derive tenant and identity only from the user

Add tenant/employee/role claims from the authenticated persisted user. Test that body/path/client-header tenant/roles cannot override the record. Finish the first stone only when its complete login tests are green.
Token tenant equals the fixture user tenant; spoofed tenant/roles do not change claims.
Reject missing tokens and forged headers

Inspect reactive hooks; strip incoming identity headers, validate bearer public-key JWT, add trusted principal fields only after verification. Test protected route without/invalid token and forged X-Tenant-Id. Keep service ports unpublished.
Anonymous/invalid token is 401 with problem shape; forged caller tenant header never reaches a business handler.
Make unknown users and wrong passwords indistinguishable

Add both negative cases with identical status/code/body shape; use dummy password verification for missing credentials and avoid exposing account state. Do not promise constant network timing; test both paths invoke an equivalent hash check.
Both cases return the same safe 401 shape and no account-existence detail.

Add bounded per-source/account attempt limits with expiry and a fixed-clock test. Use only trusted proxy address configuration, not arbitrary forwarded headers. Return 429/Retry-After; single-process limits are an honest local-deployment limit.
Threshold attempt receives 429, expiry permits retry, map has a bounded eviction policy and no plaintext login data is logged.

Inspect next unused migration version first. Persist only refresh-token hash, tenant/user/family IDs, expiry/revoked/consumed metadata and constraints/indexes. Verify clean and upgrade migrations against real PostgreSQL. No raw refresh token is stored.
Fresh/upgrade migration tests pass and DB rejects an invalid foreign tenant/user reference within the owner schema.

Issue the initial random refresh token at successful login; hash it in DB. Lock the presented token/family, mark consumed and insert successor in one transaction. Add red/green tests that one rotation succeeds and consumed predecessor cannot mint two successors.
A valid rotation returns new tokens; transaction rollback does not consume the old token; concurrent rotation cannot issue two active successors.
Revoke the family on refresh reuse

Present a consumed predecessor after a successful rotation. Revoke the whole family atomically and test that its current successor is rejected. Preserve only safe security audit metadata. No reuse is treated as a successful idempotent refresh.
Replay rejects predecessor and successor after family revocation; no second usable token escapes the race test.

Add logout family revocation using verified identity and tenant scope. Test repeated logout is harmless, another tenant family cannot be revoked, and access tokens expire within the documented short lifetime.
Logout returns documented 204 without body; refresh is denied afterward and foreign family is unaffected.

Inspect actual service methods; enable method checks and build the service principal only from the verified gateway boundary. Assert employee cannot perform HR operation and unrelated-manager resource is hidden. Do not merely hide a UI button.
Visible forbidden action returns 403; hidden foreign resource returns 404; permitted HR path succeeds.
Register every auth route in the tenant suite

Repeat the golden slice with delta: auth bootstrap exception and tenant-scoped profile/logout/refresh. Match implemented route registry to OpenAPI; test tenant B IDs, foreign-family revocation, forged headers and direct service ingress. Do not call private Docker network cryptographic identity.
Every implemented protected auth route has a negative tenant/provenance assertion; missing registry entry fails the test.

Wire authentication/authorization handlers to the shared problem contract. Assert 401, 403, 429 and malformed login errors; exclude stack traces, raw credentials and enumeration messages. Compare reactive gateway errors too.
All negative auth responses use application/problem+json and stable codes; no raw token/password/stack is present.

Add structured outcome/correlation/technical tenant fields and bounded failure/refresh-reuse counters. Test with sentinel password/token strings and assert neither appears in captured logs; tenant UUID follows approved retention/access policy.
Outcome/trace fields exist; sentinel secrets and personal identifiers are absent; metric labels do not contain user/tenant IDs.
Publish auth examples from the one contract

Update login/refresh/logout/profile examples and bearer/security rules using implemented tests. For Nuxt choose HttpOnly Secure SameSite refresh cookie with CSRF defense; access token stays in memory. Mobile uses platform secure storage, never normal preferences. Record request collection import from this contract, not a second schema.
Contract validates; safe examples contain placeholders only; web CSRF and mobile storage acceptance cases are listed.
Review the complete auth test ladder

Run the shared self-review and all auth/gateway tests including wrong password, throttling, expiry, reuse, roles, tenant/provenance and logs. If cookie/CSRF transport is not implemented, record a critical blocker; do not tag a working backend as completed web security.
All named auth cases have actual test reports; any absent required case keeps the stone/gate failed.

Inspect actual mobile root first. Add the minimal platform secure-storage adapter and one fixture proving single-flight refresh, stale-session logout once and no token in ordinary preferences/logs. Use the locked compatible secure-storage package after inspecting current platform configuration; record any native entitlement blocker. Nuxt cookie/CSRF implementation remains explicitly required, not satisfied by these mobile tests.
Selected mobile auth tests pass from confirmed root; refresh failure prompts one login without an infinite loop or token persistence leak.

Record OS/architecture, available RAM/disk, continuous uptime/power policy, operator access, backup destination and public/private ingress intent. Missing hardware is a blocker, not permission to substitute the development Mac without agreement.
Named host/resource evidence exists or deployment remains BLOCKED; no cloud machine is substituted.

Inspect existing dependency Compose and the final workload inventory. Create/review proposed selfhost manifest without secrets or published business/DB/broker ports; pin image versions/digests from actual builds and add bounded logs/health/restart. Record missing workload images explicitly.
Manifest syntax succeeds, service port inventory is private, and missing image/runtime proofs remain visible.

Separate runtime/migration roles and ignored host environment from Git. Document key identifiers/rotation procedure without values; trial test-key rollover and verify new signature accepted/old key expires as bounded policy. Check the secret scan remains enabled.
Reviewed config contains secret references only; rotation test and scan reports identify accepted/rejected test keys.

Inspect existing scripts; if absent draft only the proposed checked deploy script: validate config, require backup, record prior image/config IDs, deploy private candidate, wait bounded readiness, return nonzero on failure. No automatic volume deletion or database downgrade.
Shell syntax exits zero; shell review shows fail-fast behavior and explicit target/rollback prerequisites. This does not prove deployment.
Write the backup with an external-copy check

Inspect verified host DB/file/schema inventory. Write proposed backup script using custom pg_dump, protected private-file/config/schema inventory and encrypted external copy with checksum. Add 14-day retention only after successful new copy. Never embed credentials or delete the only backup.
Script syntax succeeds; actual backup succeeds only when dump, files, schema/replay metadata and external checksum verification all finish.
Restore to a uniquely named scratch database

Write/run the proposed scratch restore only after host and backup prerequisites. Refuse production DB/volume names. Restore roles/schema/data/files to an isolated target; compare synthetic tenant counts, login/profile and schema/config inventory. Git rollback does not reverse DB data.
Syntax passes; actual drill records pg_restore success, verified rows/auth smoke and original DB unchanged. Otherwise restore gate stays failed.
Observe private readiness and backup failure

Record health/readiness route and synthetic uptime check from private monitoring only. Trial a missing external backup destination in scratch config and verify nonzero backup/alert. Do not fill real disk or unplug production storage.
Readiness is private; synthetic missing-destination failure is visible and cannot produce a successful backup record.
Verify the public-access prerequisites stay closed

Inspect actual listener bindings and ingress plan. Confirm domain/TLS/auth/firewall/secrets/restore proofs before enabling any tunnel. Missing domain/host means private-only and failed external-access prerequisite; it is not an invitation to port-forward a DB.
Only reviewed edge binding is allowed; business/DB/broker ports are not public, and unready external access remains disabled.
Spend Thursday on the earliest failed gate

Use the buffer on one recorded auth/host/restore failure. Re-run its original command and record the minimal repair or next owner/action. No extra feature, new tool or silent reduction of the security matrix.
Earliest failure is resolved with evidence or remains the first carried action.

Repeat existing client negative fixtures: expired access, reused refresh and network interruption. Verify one login prompt, preserved unsent form data and no unbounded retry; do not add a screen today.
Existing client tests/build pass or name an exact failed assertion; no stale credential is accepted.

Run the reviewed deploy only when host/image/secrets/backup gates pass. Verify private readiness, login/profile and denied anonymous/foreign tenant requests; execute existing rollback check in scratch if rollout fails. Do not deploy red work.
Candidate reaches bounded readiness and auth smoke passes on intended host; failed rollout returns nonzero with prior release preserved.
Repeat restore and decide the weekly gate

Run the reviewed scratch restore again from the release backup, record reports and all required Q-items, map next position, commit the gate evidence and tag only if green. Stop for weekend rest; failed security/restore remains the first next action.
Restore/auth/tenant reports and actual release IDs justify PASS, or gate stays FAIL with owner/next action; nothing is prechecked.
